numerical_failure.observed_behavior: VIF values explode to extremely high numbers (quoted as 20, 40, 60, 100+) when the design matrix includes monotonic nonlinear transformations such as 1/x, log(x), 1/y, or log(y), even though there is no real multicollinearity. Related issue #6251 reports vif=inf with a zero-division warning when (1-rsquared) rounds to exactly zero, and very large finite values (e.g. 1e14, 1e20, 1e200) when ssr/tss is used instead.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: VIF should remain stable and reflect true collinearity, not inflate from numerical noise when there is no real multicollinearity. With standardize=True no spurious warnings should appear, and when the data is clean both standardize settings should return the same results (compared with rtol=1e-7). Exact expected VIF numbers are not given in the passages.
trigger_conditions: design matrix includes transformed columns such as 1/x, log(x), 1/y, or log(y) with very different numeric ranges
a plain column of 1s (constant column) mixed with columns on very different scales
variance_inflation_factor called with standardize=False (the default behaviour before the fix; standardize defaults to True after the fix)
small r_squared in the auxiliary regression so that 1-rsquared suffers floating point cancellation (issue #6251)
oracle_clues: Issue #9791 reproduction uses np.random.seed(42), n=500, x1 uniform(10,100), x2 uniform(5,50), x3 uniform(1,20) with log and inverse transforms, then calls variance_inflation_factor; the passage is truncated and gives no expected VIF values

PR #9835 adds test_vif_instability in statsmodels/stats/tests/test_influence.py with three cases: standardize=True gives stable VIFs with no warnings; standardize=False on bad data fires warnings and VIFs break; both options match on clean data

Test asserts assert_allclose(vif_true, vif_false, rtol=1e-7) on 100 rows with exog columns [ones, two normal(0,1)], variable index 1; the test uses np.random.normal without a stated seed and the exog dtype is not stated

The fix adds a standardize=True keyword argument (made keyword-only per review) to variance_inflation_factor and moves the matrix scale check to run after normalization; the passages do not give the exact r_squared clipping threshold

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: vif values of 1e14, 1e20, 1e200 are cited as essentially collinear noise; small r_squared makes (1-rsquared) round to exactly zero giving inf
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: rtol=1e-7 in test comparing standardize=True and standardize=False VIF on clean data
category_specific_evidence: Issue #6251: vif = 1/(1 - r_squared_i) with small r_squared makes (1-rsquared) exactly zero due to floating point, yielding vif=inf with zero division warning
Issue #6251: using ssr/tss instead of (1-rsquared) makes denominator floating point around zero, producing very large finite vif (e.g. 1e14, 1e20, 1e200) that are essentially collinear
Fix per PR #9835 clips r_sq before computing 1/(1-r_sq) in variance_inflation_factor, adds standardization and conditioning warning

Test asserts assert_allclose(vif_true, vif_false, rtol=1e-7) for standardize=True vs standardize=False on clean well-conditioned data with 100 rows and exog columns [ones, two normal(0,1)], variable index 1
Commit title: Fix VIF numerical instability by standardizing design matrix (closes #9791)
reproduction_risks: Passages do not state the dtype used for the exog arrays
Passages do not give the exact expected VIF values, only the comparison tolerance
Passages do not specify the exact r_squared threshold used for clipping
Test uses np.random.normal without a stated seed, so exact values are not reproducible from the passages
Keyword-only signature change (standardize) is a API preference, not a numerical property
